s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging forehead mass with possible intracranial extension
salient_findings: A 10 cm × 8 cm soft, compressible mass on the right forehead
A palpable bony step-off at the base of the mass
Intracranial extension and possible involvement of the superior sagittal sinus on MRI
key_facts: The lesion appeared 1 year after minor forehead trauma
The mass slowly enlarged over the past 4 months without pain or other symptoms
The patient has a history of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma of the left foot
The patient underwent below-knee amputation and adjuvant ifosfamide-doxorubicin chemotherapy 9 years earlier
The mass is located on the right forehead, extending from the hairline to the mid-forehead
The mass is soft and compressible
A full-thickness skin and frontalis incision exposed a gray, well-circumscribed mass
Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a mass arising from the right frontal diploic space
Noncontrast head CT revealed a lytic lesion of the right frontal bone with hypodense soft-tissue extension into the scalp

shortlist.label: Chordoma with intracranial extension
shortlist.why_kept: The mass is located on the right forehead with intracranial extension and possible involvement of the superior sagittal sinus, consistent with chordoma

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has a history of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and the current mass has a lytic lesion of the right frontal bone, raising concern for osteosarcoma

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has a history of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and the current mass is a slowly enlarging forehead mass, consistent with chondrosarcoma

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has a history of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and the current mass has a lytic lesion of the right frontal bone, raising concern for metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: The mass is a slowly enlarging forehead mass with a soft and compressible texture, consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans

raw.rationale: The patient's history of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and the appearance of a new mass in a different location, with imaging findings showing a lytic lesion and intracranial extension, suggests metastatic disease as the most likely explanation.

rejected.label: Chordoma with intracranial extension
rejected.why: No specific evidence of chordoma characteristics in the vignette

rejected.why: The mass is described as soft and compressible, which is not typical of osteosarcoma

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of chondrosarcoma, the new mass's location and characteristics do not strongly suggest a primary chondrosarcoma
